exercises.prompt: How many fard prayers are there each day?
exercises.explanation: Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib and Isha - five anchors that structure the whole day.

source.text: Prayer has been decreed upon the believers at specified times.

exercises.prompt: Which pillar of Islam is the one that immediately follows the testimony of faith?
exercises.explanation: The Prophet built Islam on five: shahada, prayer, zakat, fasting and Hajj - prayer comes first after belief.

source.text: Islam is built upon five: the testimony of faith, the prayer, zakat, the fast of Ramadan and the pilgrimage.

exercises.prompt: What is khushu?
exercises.explanation: The Quran opens Surah al-Mu’minun with the successful believers - those humble in their prayer.

source.text: Those who are humble in their prayer.

options.text: Presence of heart and humility during prayer
Raising the voice so others hear

source.text: Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers at specified times.

options.text: Any personal dua made during the day

exercises.prompt: Arrange the steps of preparing for prayer in the correct order.
exercises.explanation: Before prayer: purify your body, clothes and place, perform wudu, face the qiblah, make the intention in your heart, then begin with the takbir.

source.text: O you who believe, when you rise to pray, wash your faces and your forearms to the elbows, wipe over your heads and wash your feet to the ankles.

steps.text: Make sure your body, clothes and place of prayer are clean
Make the intention (niyyah) in your heart
Raise your hands and say the opening takbir

exercises.prompt: Where does the niyyah (intention) of prayer live?
exercises.explanation: The intention is the heart’s orientation - the Prophet and his Companions never announced it aloud.

source.text: Actions are only judged by intentions, and every person will have what he intended.

options.text: In the words announced out loud

exercises.prompt: Which three things must be clean before you point your prayer mat toward the qiblah?
exercises.explanation: Purification covers the person, the garment and the ground - the earth itself is a place of purification for the ummah.

source.text: The earth has been made for me a place of worship and a means of purification.

options.text: Body, clothes and place of prayer

exercises.prompt: Which direction do Muslims face in prayer?
exercises.explanation: Allah commanded the turning to al-Masjid al-Haram; every mosque’s mihrab marks that direction.

source.text: So turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram; wherever you are, turn your faces toward it.

options.text: Toward the Ka’bah in Makkah - the qiblah

exercises.prompt: You are praying behind an imam. When do you move?
exercises.explanation: The imam is appointed to be followed: you say takbir after his takbir, bow after he bows.

source.text: The imam is to be followed: say the takbir when he says it, bow when he bows, prostrate when he prostrates.

options.text: Whenever you finish your own recitation
You follow the imam - never moving before him
Half a second before him to be ready

exercises.prompt: Put the five daily prayers in time order, starting with the first.
exercises.explanation: Allah fixed five prayers across the day: Fajr at dawn, Dhuhr after midday, Asr in the afternoon, Maghrib just after sunset, and Isha at night.

source.text: Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers at specified times.

exercises.prompt: Which prayer comes just after midday?
exercises.explanation: The working day pauses: Dhuhr is established when the sun passes its highest point.

source.text: Establish prayer at the decline of the sun.

exercises.prompt: What did the Prophet compare the five daily prayers to?
exercises.explanation: The river simile makes the math easy: sins wash off as the prayer-cycle repeats.

source.text: If there was a river at your door and you bathed in it five times a day, would any dirt remain? That is the case with the five prayers.

options.text: A river at your door, washing away dirt five times a day

exercises.prompt: You oversleep and miss Asr entirely. What should you do?
exercises.explanation: Missing a prayer through sleep or forgetfulness is prayed the moment it is remembered - no penalty beyond that.

source.text: Whoever forgets a prayer or sleeps through it, let him pray it when he remembers it.

options.text: Wait for next year’s same day
Pray it as soon as you remember

exercises.prompt: Which prayer comes at dawn, before sunrise?
exercises.explanation: The Quran calls it the recitation of dawn - witnessed by angels as the day opens.

source.text: Establish prayer at the decline of the sun until the darkness of night, and the recitation of dawn - indeed it is witnessed.

exercises.prompt: Arrange what happens inside one rakah in the correct order.
exercises.explanation: The Prophet taught the steps of a rakah: takbir, reciting al-Fatihah and a short surah, bowing, rising, then two prostrations with a sitting between them.

source.text: The Prophet taught the man who prayed badly: when you stand for prayer say the takbir, then recite, then bow until at rest, then rise, then prostrate until at rest...

steps.text: Recite a short surah (in the first two rakahs)
Sit up between the two prostrations

exercises.prompt: What concludes the prayer?
exercises.explanation: As the takbir opens the prayer, the taslim closes it - peace spoken to the sides and to the angels.

source.text: The key of the prayer is purification, its opening is the takbir, and its closing is the taslim.

options.text: The salam - turning to the right and left: "As-salamu alaykum wa rahmatullah"

exercises.prompt: What begins the prayer?
exercises.explanation: The takbir marks the boundary: before it you move freely, after it you are standing before Allah.

source.text: When you stand for prayer, say the takbir, then recite...

exercises.prompt: What is said while prostrating (sujud)?
exercises.explanation: Sujud is the closest a servant comes to Allah - and the words glorify Him as the Most High.

source.text: The Prophet prostrated saying: Glory to my Lord the Most High.

exercises.prompt: What is said while bowing (ruku)?
exercises.explanation: Ruku glorifies Allah as the Supreme One; sujud glorifies Him as the Most High - each posture has its own words.

source.text: The Prophet bowed saying: Glory to my Lord the Supreme.

exercises.prompt: Which surah is recited in every single rakah?
exercises.explanation: There is no prayer for the one who does not recite the Opening of the Book - al-Fatihah is the heartbeat of every rakah.

source.text: There is no prayer for the one who does not recite the Opening of the Book (al-Fatihah).

exercises.prompt: Your mind wanders mid-prayer. What is the first practical step?
exercises.explanation: Khushu is a practice of returning - awareness drifts, and the trained heart brings it back to the words.

source.text: Those who are humble and focused in their prayer.

options.text: Return your attention to the words you are saying

exercises.prompt: Standing hurts because of illness. What does the Sunnah allow?
exercises.explanation: Islam is ease: the Prophet’s guidance adapts prayer to ability rather than dropping it.

source.text: Pray standing; if you cannot, then sitting; if you cannot, then lying on your side.

options.text: Pray sitting, and if you cannot, then lying on your side

exercises.prompt: What did the Prophet say about a prayer rushed without its essential parts?
exercises.explanation: The man who prayed badly was taught the full sequence - rushing strips a prayer to the bone.

source.text: The Prophet made the man who rushed his prayer repeat it, and taught him each part until he did it properly.
